newsitem.title: Russia: Yeltsin to meet Duma speaker Seleznyov - agency.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin to meet Duma speaker Seleznyov - agency.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin will meet the speaker of the State Duma, Russia's lower house of parliament, on Monday, Interfax news agency said, quoting parliamentary sources.

The Kremlin press service could not confirm the meeting, which Interfax earlier said had already taken place at the Barvikha sanatorium outside Moscow, where the president is convalescing from his November 5 heart bypass operation.
The agency said the two men were to discuss a variety of legislation and the peace process in Chechnya as well as, possibly, the political crisis in Belarus.

The Duma, dominated by the communist opposition, decided on Sunday to call a special debate next Friday on Yeltsin's weekend order to pull the remaining Russian troops out of Chechnya and seal a peace accord giving the region wide-ranging autonomy.
Seleznyov, who took part in Russia's failed conciliation efforts in Belarus last week, is a communist.
The party advocates the restoration in some form of the Soviet Union and is hotly opposed to anything that smacks of the break-up of the Russia Federation's territorial integrity.
Communist leader Gennady Zyuganov accused Yeltsin of treason on Sunday and said the peace accord would create a "malignant tumour" in Chechnya which would affect the whole country.
Despite the strength of communists and nationalists in the Duma, parliament has little power to overturn government policy.

RIA news agency quoted Kremlin chief-of-staff Anatoly Chubais as saying Yeltsin might also meet Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin on Monday. The premier is due to fly to Paris in the evening for an official visit.
